input_text: So... I was very excited when I found this game. Not only because it's exactly the kind of game I was looking for, but also because the price was so reasonable. I just finished my first play-through and I did really enjoy it although I do have some comments & concerns about gameplay. I saw before purchasing that a lot of people insisted this game needed some kind of tutorial & that has been fixed, I found the tutorial to be super helpful. I do agree with another commenter though that a guided-victory tutorial (rather than a show & tell tutorial) would be much more beneficial. I did have to lose the game twice before I realized how to properly strategize with the available faith. After I figured out exactly what I was doing, it was much more enjoyable. It would be GREAT if the abilities tab was bigger or if you could just select abilities from the drawer, rather than having to drag them into the main panel. I would also love it if it was possible to continue playing after winning the game. Yes, all objectives have been met by the time you win, but I would still love to be able to completely conquer the map even if there is no added benefit to doing so. I'd also love to see some tiered advancement. For example "Win as [someone], unlock [something], Start with [country], unlock [something], etc.". Just something to motivate further playing since once you've run through all the Gods, you're just playing the same game over again. Just a note, not a huge deal. All in all, this is a fantastic game & I'm excited I found it. It was a little difficult getting in because, like I said, the tutorial was a good guide but not super helpful in actual gameplay, but once you figure it out it's a great way to kill some time.

input_text: This DLC is mainly for those who have already completed the main game, unlocked everything possible, and completed the demonic difficulty with at least 5-6 tokens. Each heroine gets her own alternative version (8 new characters in total), which is a little more powerful due to, as a rule, a longer weapon range and powerful abilities. However, their weapons are not quite simple, but tied to each character, so they cannot be changed or improved as in the base game. A new level that opens after completing all the levels of the base game. Which is good, it is far from easy, more powerful and unpleasant opponents, sometimes even bosses from previous levels appear. With good build and items you can pass, but if not - it will be almost impossible. Adds several relics and scrolls from bosses. Overall, I really liked it, spent a lot of time in it. True, I expected the new bosses to be stronger. Of the cons, probably, the price is half the cost of the base game. But if you liked the game - get the DLC too, you will not regret it.

input_text: Experienced on Windows Mixed Reality This is one of the worst platformers I have ever played in VR. I'm just surprised it has any positive reviews. I was only able to play about 30 minutes before the game hard crashed (had to restart Windows). I took that as a sign that I should quit and uninstall this garbage. I don't even want to do a video review for this mess of a game. First of all, it ran poorly on my 1060 GTX. Controls (gamepad) felt sluggish to respond (motion controllers are only used at the hub menu to select items). The rollergirls start out very slow from the gate. You feel like you're skating on molasses. The visuals are dated with poor lighting and textures. The camera views are very poor. There's these parts where you ride vehicles. You're in third person view in VR while riding these vehicles and your AI friends obstruct your view. It's a simple game of Frogger during these portions of the game. Collect cows (save them from aliens) and avoid getting hit. The side scrolling is almost as bad. You have a small field of view. You basically switch in and out of the different roller girls to take down enemies. Freeze it, switch and throw a missile at the alien enemies. There's some powerups that increase your speed and some upgrades that make your weapon stronger. Unfortunately, the game runs poorly, the controls aren't responsive enough, and the environments and level design are dull and uninspired. This honestly feels like the quality of a 2013-15 free to play mobile game. It's running on the Unity Engine. It looks & plays ugly. Scantily-clad women on roller skates cannot save it. Rate 3/10. Unfortunately, I bought this back in a 2017 Steam sale for $4 USD and I didn't play it until now. Too late for a refund, but don't make the same mistake I did. Do NOT buy this game. You've been warned! If you enjoyed reading my review. please consider joining my Steam Curator Group here: [URL]

input_text: Fritz for Fun 13 is the best chess program I have played. Prior to this I played fritz 5.32 as white and Windows chess as black. In friend mode the program is quite sharp without being impossible. I've only played 3 games so far and each of them was very instructive. Fritz pushes the margin and makes you think. It doesn't play mechanically where you have to survive 20 moves then it makes an obvious blunder. It plays a full game and not a gauntlet you have to survive through. The 3d chess pieces and manual board orientation offers the perfect viewing angle as if you yourself were leaning over a chess board pondering. It offers a lot of tools for practice and such but I play chess for fun and am not too critical. The evaluation profile window and the main engine window with the control board are staples of fritz for reviewing your games to see how you did. For positions where you don't understand why the computer uses the line it does in the main engine window you can use the analysis options to analyse a given position and it will show the branches saying why this and that doesn't work. The only downside to Fritz for Fun 13 is it only supports one core. The only real downside to that is you can't use the 8 core Houdini engine to evaluate an opening in great depth and see what works and what doesn't(This is assuming you know the basic openings e.g. kings gambit declined, pirc, english, dutch ect.). You can get around that however by downloading the Arena GUI and running 8 core houdini from that. Conclusion: Perfect game if you like playing chess for fun; this is to say you play to match your wits against the computer and not to memorize chess databases and pantomime. After playing 13 games against the engine I found the friend mode to be too soft compared with fritz 5.32. You can blunder your way through a game and still win. With 5.32 I've played about 500 games and win on average 1 in 5. With fritz 13 I've played 13 games and have won 4 and lost 1. The longest time spent on one move might be 5 minutes. Longest game might be 20 minutes. I've played 50 minute games against 5.32 because it creates more difficult positions and if you make a single mistake you lose unless you are better than the base engine which I am not. Also it seems the fritz 13 engine has disappeared entirely. I only have the option to use the fritz 6 engine. The only way I have been able to get it back is to do a second install with the setup file which spreads files across multiple hard-drives. I played another game against fritz and lost my queen at the beginning of the game and was down -6 and still managed to end up with a draw. I think I was even +3 eventually. I played another game where I had hanging pieces(trying out a new chess set) and the computer didn't capture them. Brutally obvious captures on the control board the computer ignores. Move two it can make 5 viable moves from each of its previous 5 viable moves. Continuing with induction by move 4 there is 625 move combinations(identifying the permutations is labor intensive). input_text: Alpha/EA first impressions: This is sort of the RTS version of what Torchlight is to RPG/Diablo-esque games. It's arcadey and a little cartoony but it's fun and even the alpha/EA version runs well and has a variety of game modes even if certain things are placeholder or a little sparse still. You can have up to 3 Servos in battle along with 15-20 or so drones in a typical skirmish. There are several different types of drones, eco and armoury upgrades, turrets, unit producing factories, healing beacons, some neutral roaming monsters and different economy nodes around the map to capture. There's a variety of gear and parts you can earn and swap around on your Servos between games to go for certain playstyles. It will have a campaign/SP side on release and has MP and Co-Op already. I'd like to see it get a bit more depth and character as it develops. It is a little too generic/cartoony for my tastes aesthetically right now but, again, it's an alpha and there's a lot more to be added so I'm curious where they will take it. Update: Changing my review to a thumbs down. One of my few Early Access regrets. It's been many months since my initial review and there's been zero communication from the devs on what's happening with the game. There was a single small update in the past 6 months. The game stopped working on my new W10 PC and support was not able to find a reason or solution. I've completely lost interest in the game and it seems the devs have as well...

input_text: (Updated 9th Mar 2017) When I first reviewed Duck Force I gave it a Thumbs Down because of what I felt was a poorly implemented representation of a certain bodily function. Thanks to a recent update this issue has been well and truly put to bed. Not only that, but the dev has made available a free demo, so there is now officially NO REASON for duckophiles (or those who are merely duck-curious) to not give Duck Force a go. And give it a go you should. Duck Force is a VR game with nice cartoony graphics, decent (and amusing) audio and a novel control method which is difficult to describe, because there is no other game I know of that I can compare it to. Basically, you point (in 3D space) your Vive controller in the direction you want the duck to fly. You can also make the duck instantly do a 180, or speed him up (with the awesome power that is DUCK FARTS) or slow him right down (with the power of I don't know what. It's probably just a duck thing. Go ask a duck.) The duck can also, in much the same way as a real life duck, shoot projectiles out of its head, which can obliterate environmental hazards, particulary wooden structures with coins inside them, which makes them easier for the duck to collect. Collecting coins is such an original and unique concept, I am surprised that it has never been implemented in any other game. You can also shoot down bunny rabbits, who are apparently hostile towards the duck, so they deserve to die. The duck's military capabilities enable it to to mete out tough justice against the rabbits, and rightly so. Your duck will however die, and die often. It's easy to die because coming into contact with anything which is not collectible or fly-throughable will result in a dead duck. Which is as funny as fuck, the duck just splats against some inanimate object while a couple of yellow feathers float forlornly to the ground. It's OK though, because your duck is immortal, just like a real duck, and you can shoot him back into the air with a quick flick of a trigger finger. You can bet that vengeance will be his. There is other stuff to do as well, like flying through rings, which is fun, and lets you test out your flying skills. Real ducks do this kind of thing all the time, can you elevate your skills to that level? Probably not, as ducks are an awesome force of nature, but it's something to aspire to. TL;DR You should AT LEAST try the demo. It's free ffs. If you don't like it, accept that you hate ducks, life and yourself and go play some lame dating sim. Otherwise, buy Duck Force and support the guy who is doing good things in VR, listens to customer feedback, and, most importantly, LIKES DUCKS. PS My original review of Duck Force appears below, I gave it a Thumbs Down at the time. I've left it in for historical reasons, but you can pretty much ignore its content because it's mainly just me whining about one thing that has since been fixed. Read it if you want, but it will be a complete waste of time. Time that would be better spent downloading the Duck Force demo and becoming one with your inner duck. ****************** START ORIGINAL REVIEW ********************* I bought this game primarily because it's got a duck in it, and I feel that devs who make games with ducks in them are deserving of my support. There is a lot to like about this game, the graphics look good, the flight mechanics are weird but OK, and of course, the protagonist is a duck. Unfortunately I just can't recommend this right now because of one fatal flaw - it is, literally too "in your face". See, the best way to play this is by flying around with the duck. He flies along right in front of you which is fine, but the problem is that when you speed him up he FARTS RIGHT IN YOUR FACE! input_text: Its the GOAT. If you know, you know. Game runs incredibly well, everything cranked to the max, including ray tracing. I am running a 4090 though, but even without ray tracing it looks incredible. Enough has changed that more than once I was caught off guard, but then again, I hadn't played through the game in probably 15 years. A lot of the same old tricks that worked in the OG still work here. If you've never played a Resident Evil game, or are sensitive to scares, this is a great one to start with. The RE2/3 remake are quite "scary". This one is just right. Everything feels really well tuned. The old tank controls are gone and replaced with something a bit more modern. There are some changes I didnt love, but got used to, like the knife having durability that diminishes and breaks after so much use. Another thing that was hard to get used to was the fact that your aiming reticle is no longer a laser sight, and is replaced with cross hairs. You still have the same kind of recoil and what not, but now you have to deal with bloom. Either way, I quickly got past both of those two "issues" and very quickly forgot about them. All in all, 10/10 game. 10/10 for a remake/remaster.

I don't know how many hours I have logged on the 360 of AC... so I will say, going into this was a bit odd, not having all the combat capabilities that you start out with in the sequel, but I was also a bit lost in it by not having the context from AA. But nothing will beat the claustrophobia of Arkham Asylum, the neverending hallways, the sleeper agent Asylum chime; the first time you get out of Intensive Treatment and onto the Island. The giant greenish moon, the constant chattering from "Warden Joker". I do prefer the plot of City, and one could argue the ending in Asylum was a bit anticlimactic in comparison but the aesthetic was perfect in Asylum. Once I replay City (again times 5) I do believe having this game under my belt will make the experience ten times better. To close, don't ask how many screenshots I took of Joker while playing through this. Just don't. I'm vengeance.

input_text: You're getting what you pay for with this DLC. Dozens and dozens of ways to make Dungeonmans a more challenging experience. I have to give the DLC major props for not just going to road of number bloat. While you can modify monster stats (as well as just about every numerical mechanic in the game) by X% if you so desire, also present are a multitude of ways to add additional mechanics to the game to make things more challenging. Weapon breakage, armor destruction, starvation, fatigue, enemies that explode on death and more are present as unique mechanics whose sole purpose is to make your life miserable. All of the above modifiers stack to provide a Brutality™ score that ties in to new leaderboards that were provided for the DLC specifically in addition to those recently added to the base game. Weekly Pay2Lose runs are also featured with the DLC, for those who like to compete on a large scale against other players for the highest score. input_text: When I saw this being played on Twitch, I immediately was reminded of a game I used to play on my TI-83 in my highschool years called "Blockdude". I'm a huge fan of DOS, Amiga, Apple II, Atari ST, etc. puzzle games, and this is a definite throwback to those. I discovered that Blockman actually predates the game I played, so I checked the shareware version out on a Dosbox page, and I definitely see the 'inspiration'! Kudos on getting permission from Blockman's dev to do this game! Anyways, I've played through most of the levels and absolutely love this game, The first 10 levels are fairly easy but the difficulty ramps up nicely. I was worried after the first couple levels that this was going to be an easy game, but the later levels put those worries to rest. A few suggestions/feedback: - Add more music. The menu and gameplay songs are great, but would like a few more gameplay songs - The manual is well-written, but many people might not even notice the link for the manual, so an in-game tutorial might be helpful - Level sharing through ModDB / IndieDB works well, but Steam Workshop integration would be even better Overall, love this game and highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys retro games and very thinky puzzle games. Warning, it is very difficult, especially the later half of the main levels and all of the bonus levels, but it is a welcome challenge.

input_text: I've read and enjoyed a fair few Ebihime VNs by this point, but I can't really recommend this one. Store page says it's a medieval fantasy but there's nothing medieval about it -- certainly not the character art nor the backgrounds. The worldbuilding is quite generic, and better background art could have done a lot of the heavylifting in terms of making the world feel real. The use of photos for backgrounds with extremely stylised sprites is a visually unpleasant combination in my opinion, particularly since no effort was made to remove obviously modern touches from the backgrounds. It's very anime inspired -- you can see it in the character tropes, behaviour, and even the sound effects used in their speech. With how disjointed this visual novel was, it just added another layer of confusion to a rather jumbled mixture of elements. I did like how different routes revealed different bits of information about the events in the first part of the game. I found some of the characters obnoxious, and the dialogue tedious at times. All in all, this one's kind of a miss for me.

input_text: As a avid player of Match-3 games, and appreciator of the Puzzle Quest saga, I convinced myself to give Runespell: Overture a shot, intrigued by the fact you play with a standard deck of cards instead of coloured gems. The first battles were interesting, the poker-like combos felt novel. Diving more deeply into the game, it got more depth with the addition of magic cards and sidekicks. Unfortunately, it appeared that most of the magic cards are just copies of the same basic spell (unlike other games where fire, ice, lightning and poison have different tactical effects). From that point, the battles felt too much similar to sustain interest, and the constant sight of these clubs, diamonds, hearts and spades turned the fantasy background into the trivial one your regular Solitaire. These kind of games are supposed to be easy to develop on a reasonable budget, deliberately limiting fancy graphics to focus solely on gameplay depth. Sadly, this game is a living testimony of a team being too lazy or too tired to make a truly great game. Maybe they lost faith in this game at some point. No wonder this happened to me too.

input_text: There probably isn't a franchise i've collectively spent more hours in since watching my brother play Civilization 3 when i was a kid, and my brother then installing Civilization 2 on our dad's ancient computer for me. Thousands of collective hours. I've always been open and positive about the changes each game has introduced, in the face of much flaming negative feedback from the general civilization community. I remember people being furious at the swap to hexagons in 5, hating city states. I remember people hating Civilization 6 on launch (which, granted, was a little deserved), but i still played both games with a positive attitude, knowing it'd improve. It was still Civilization at it's core after all. And, i was right, since Civilization 6 is my most played game on record (as of writing). And then comes Civilization 7. Promising first looks in the early preview footage, i love the rivers, the evolving of civilizations seems wonderful. But the thing that strikes me the worst is of course, the price tag. I'm not ashamed to say i bought the most expensive deluxe pre-purchase, for again, this series is a part of me, i'll allow myself this. Still, this absurd idea of charging this much for games nowadays is a trend publishers need to stop falling for immediately. But regardless. Game releases, i've been talking for months about how my life will be dedicated to this game for a few weeks. I play it, i like it, but, it just fatigues me. I'm not sure what, but. I only play it for a few days, maybe. And nothing really compels me to pick it up again. I could be tired of the formula, but. I dunno. I think it's just, too far from what i really enjoy about old Civ. Like, i wish we got a more traditional Civ with like, the army mechanics, the rivers, the towns. I dunno. I'm not giving up hope, but, maybe i should. 2K as a company can eat my whole ass, after Kerbal Space Program 2. And this EVOLVE level of price hiking. If Firaxis really cares, tone back the egregious DLC model, and release either several free updates to fix the game, i know you are capable of it, you managed to patch together Civ6 just fine. Or release one or two SOLID DLC to improve things. And for gods sake diversify the amount of civilizations available. There's SO FEW. CLASSICS that have been in the game since the start are missing, and you make BRITAIN a DLC? Come on. Pull yourselves together, Firaxis.

input_text: I guess my opinion is different from the majority, as this game has overall positive reviews. I didn't like the story, graphics, gameplay or the music. In my opinion it's a very depressing game and I don't recommend it. There are several parts where there are no hints and I could not progress without looking up online how to do something, and had to repeat the same scene several times from the start, with no option to skip cutscenes I had already seen. Some of the scenes are very slow with very little action or anything that adds to the story, I felt bored and frustrated a lot of the time. There is no consequence for death, you just respawn instantly, so the enemies don't feel threatening, instead you just die over and over until you progress. The graphics are overly pixellated, and objects in the background and atmospheric effects have a higher resolution than the main sprites, which is a strange design choice, and one I'm not a fan of. If you're going for pixel graphics, my preference is to do it as if it's on an 8-bit or 16-bit console, and keep the pixel sizes consistent, Shovel Knight is a good example. The narration felt like it was trying to push a world view regarding pain and suffering. I guess some people enjoy wallowing in misery? The music is nearly all in the minor key, with slow melancholic piano and violins. The sound effects are decent, and change depending on the surroundings, e.g. echoing if you go inside a cave, I appreciate this and more games should have better sound design. The length of the game is very short, I completed it in 4 hours even though I got stuck and back tracked multiple times. Some of the story scenes didn't make much sense and I felt like the game was unfinished and didn't explain everything; there were some loose ends. I think I expected it to be more like Hollow Knight or Ori and the Blind Forest, just a nice platforming game, but it's not really that. It's more trying to tell a story using a game as the medium instead of a film or book. I just think it fell short of its promise and could have done more as a game. SPOILERS - scenes from the game and ending: You play as 3 characters, an old man, a young girl and a knight. The young girl scenes were slow, and require you to examine everything in each room multiple times to find something the game wants you to interact with. Then you get a cut scene hinting about domestic abuse and kidnapping, but the distressing scenes turn out to be not quite what the game makes out at first. I won't give the story away, but in the girl's mind she sees one thing and the reality is different as she doesn't have all the facts. The scene I was stuck on was getting into the attic; there was no hint that I needed an item from downstairs. The old man scenes require you to solve puzzles and do a bit more platforming, where there are enemies to avoid, this is ok, but there was a lot of frustrating back tracking and no hints about how to get the black heart to fix the elevator. There were a couple of scenes where I died over and over as this character, as the enemy sometimes spawns right in front of you, or a bat just keeps knocking you off a platform. The knight scenes had more action and you can kill enemies with a sword and use a grappling hook to traverse obstacles. It would have been great if they just ran with this concept and fleshed it out more with some boss fights and upgrades, but the serpent boss at the end was only a cutscene. The keeper, the main antagonist, isn't really explained, and I didn't 100% understand the fountain scene and so the game felt unfinished, as I had hoped everything would tie in together and explain the bigger picture.

Right off the bat, the map is overcrowded with obstacles to be cleared, which would be fun enough, however your character is not attached to the grid system everything else is on. There is only one person you can talk to from the start of the game and he gives you a quest to go into the caves to collect ingredients for a potion, which appears to be necessary to talk to the people in town. As in, you can not go into town until you make the potion. I did not get to that point though as the combat system is clunky and intuitive. Don't worry though, there is no health in the game, so you can't be killed as the monsters move back and forth in front of and through you as you try to figure out how the fire ball spell works. input_text: The Curse of Badly Localized Visual Novels Claims Another Victim... Sadly, I can't fully recommend this short Boys Love Visual Novel, therefore my review can pretty much be considered as a neutral one. I still decided to give it a thumbs up because of the touching narrative and the nice artwork. The writing, however, just has too many issues and is obviously in need of both proofreading and editing. Yun , our protagonist, is deeply concerned about his best friend Max , which got badly injured in an accident and lies in a coma ever since. Yun visits him every day, not only out of concern, or because he is romantically attracted to him, but also because he's able to talk and interact with his friend since Yun has the ability to enter Max's dreams. The only thing Yun needs to do is to fall asleep near him. There is no obvious clarification as to why he is able to visit the dreams of the comatose Max, but one route explains the circumstances for that, at least, vaguely. The book Yun reads describes that people who are really close to each other are able to enter the other person's dreams, as long as the feelings are strong enough. It's more elaborated in the game, and the book furthermore explains a way to save the person who lies in a coma. The results of that can be witnessed in one ending. Of course, it's up to you if this explanation is satisfying enough or not. [URL] Talking about endings, May has several of them, but none can be considered as happy or even good to begin with, which is quite depressing as you may imagine. Every outcome leaves a bitter taste, there isn't a single ending that makes up for it. You should be aware of this before you give this Visual Novel a try. I do know that there are people that simply can't handle bad endings well if there is no happy end in sight that compensates the reader for suffering. The story ultimately revolves around loss, sorrow, and how to deal with the feeling that you might have only little time left to spend with someone very dear to you. Honestly, this is the kind of story that usually makes me sob like a little girl, but this time I just felt nothing. No tears were shed, and the story touched me only a tiny bit. I'm pretty sure that the cause for that is the bad writing that just kind of failed to get me in the mood to actually care about the characters. [URL] The English translation, or rather the localization, was handled pretty badly. I felt irritation building up while playing May . Don't get me wrong, you can catch the meaning perfectly, but especially if a Visual Novel tries to pull on your heartstrings, which May clearly does, it slightly fails to do that if not a single sentence is written correctly, at least that's what I think. It just makes it hard for me to take the story seriously, and since the story provided here is more heart-wrenching and serious than anything else, the bad localization regrettably ruined every tad of atmosphere for me. Except for the bad translation itself, it is also very confusing when the character names change rapidly between fore and last name, or when they address the protagonist simply as the guy . May's story could be so touching if it wouldn't be for this single, yet deal-breaking issue. I'm very sorry that I mention it so often but it's the sole reason why I couldn't immerse myself into the story, which makes me terribly sad since the storyline alone is absolutely great. The transition of all seasons in the main menu is really pretty, even if you might don't see much of that since you will most likely finish this game in one sitting, taken how short it is. Nevertheless, it's still a nice feature, which I'd like to point out after complaining so much about the writing. The artwork is surprisingly nice as well, especially if you consider that this title only costs $3.99. The CGs of Yun and his mother when she's trying to comfort him really touched my heart on a level I honestly didn't expect. input_text: I saw someone say that this is a good game to play when you don't know what to do with your life, and so I expected the story to be about the meaning of life, and yeah, it is that, but it's also so much more. It's very well thought out not only on philosophical level but also political, sociological, even environmental, the story is heavily focused on morals and values of people, what is considered good and how big the lesser evil can be before it's just good ol' plain evil. And the way these themes were presented through a detective-like, detail focused (I mean, you have to not just listen to the characters talk, you HAVE to remember what they're saying and utilize it in a smart manner in the future) main plot with jaw dropping twists, genuinely entertaining side plots, well lived in world-building where I didn't question its reality for a second, and through great combination of 3D environments and 2D animations, fun little combat encounters and incredibly engaging 4th wall breaking, is absolutely incredible. This game needs a follow up story, an anime, a fucking movie I don't care, its so so fantastic I need more from this world. The only minus is that considering how much this game relies on text I do believe more proofreading should've been done for the ENG translation because there are grammar mistakes scattered throughout the game heavily on top of the conversations sometimes losing their meaning due to the said meaning being lost in translation. This was a gem i stumbled upon accidentally and I will always thank the algorithm gods for that.

input_text: EDIT: While initially I didn't recommend, I do think the game is good and I was a bit too harsh. The game has potential, is updated regularly, and the developer is receptive to input. That is all anyone could ask for in a game. Something that I forgot to mention was that the gameplay loop is relatively quick, which I think is a strength. Big win in my eyes as it felt like an auto loss before when they spawned I look forward to where the game goes. ------------------ Novi Cube is a neat concept but suffers from poor execution. The level up mechanic is flawed. You pick one of three random traits offered and have the option to reroll for a "token", something you get for clearing bosses. However, a bunch of these traits are useless. Projectile size does basically nothing. Explosive tiles are ineffective against bosses. There is a very clear meta that forms as you attempt higher difficulties. I find myself taking the same upgrades every time because everything else just doesn't have the damage. Not only that but the black hole enemy sucks out all the fun you might have. It exerts gravity, eats your shots and is invulnerable so you are essentially helpless if it spawns. It doesn't even give you anything if you survive it. God help you if the game decides to position you right under it, you will never be able to break any tiles. Did I forget to mention that you can't even control where you shoot from?

input_text: Review with accompanying screenshots and video in Sinical Network [URL] Dead Wishes is independent developer VIOLET Studio Games's first visual novel in Steam and itch.io, featuring an adult romance thriller supernatural narrative, a genderless protagonist with a customizable name, and a large cast of male and female characters. Story and Characters The story begins with the main character (default name is Dante) on the verge of being kicked out of their rented apartment for being late in their rental payments. Dante will then get to know the residents of the unnamed city and develop a relationship with them, taking you through various scenarios depending on the choices you make. Maybe you will join the mafia where you uncover a heated love affair gone wrong, become allied with a team of murderers, serve as a caretaker for two dysfunctional sisters, end up on the streets, or become an honest man yourself. Your decisions throughout the story will dictate whether you find love and happiness, or face a dire outcome, but playing through all the routes will piece together the full story. The characters are sufficiently different from one another, each with their own backstories. Some characters will know others to varying degrees, and they will react differently to Dante depending on the route chosen. Some romanceable characters may also turn up as enemies in certain character routes, adding to the thriller aspect, and the degree of immersion into the game. I must admit, I love romantic comedies, honest to goodness stories, and happy endings, so I like Clement and Festus's routes for fitting into this category. Most of the other character routes and endings tend to be darker and may involve killing other characters or Dante. Still, I can appreciate the scriptwriter for taking the time to explain the character motivations for killing someone, giving each character variable shades of grey in their personalities, and allowing Dante to change that character for the better to add a further degree of immersion into the story. As such, I also like Allegra, Anise, Eira, Nanako, Ophelia, and Sergio's routes despite the darker and violent storytelling. The remaining characters are too dark and yandere-ish for me to appreciate fully, although I would still give props to the scriptwriter for exploring this aspect. Audio and Visuals The BGM is decent with each character having their own musical track, and over the course of the story, there is a mix of pleasant, sinister, or fast-paced music appropriate for the amount of tension in the scene. I like Morning Espresso (Allegra's theme), Omertà (Sergio's theme), Snowy Fair (Eira's theme), Baked (Clement's theme), and The Last Dance (Anise's theme) for bringing out the respective character's mystery and nature. The other BGM such as Twelve, Introspection, Past, A Moment's Peace, A Lonely Alley, Mistake, and One also help to convey the mood in the story. The CGs are fine for the most part, although since this visual novel places more emphasis on storytelling, each character is limited to 3 CGs that are more or less predictable after completing a few character routes. I also like the developer for using a different coloured diamond shaped icon with an arrow moving to the left or right when a dialogue choice is made to show the change in that character's disposition towards Dante. Replayability This visual novel has 12 character routes, most of which have 3 endings altogether, and a memories section to help players keep track of the endings unlocked. A downloadable PDF guide is also available at the developer's website to help players obtain all endings and learn more about the characters. As the story progresses, the mysterious person on the title screen will show themselves and reveal a surprise and additional post-ending story for all 12 characters, giving that motivation to attempt all the endings and enjoy the high replay value in the game, despite the absence of Steam achievements. It is a shame that the game only has 24 save slots even though there are so many routes, dialogue choices and endings in the game. Overall thoughts After spending close to 10 hours to read and listen through the text and dialogue, Dead Wishes is an interesting plot-focused adult thriller romance visual novel with dark supernatural themes and additional surprises spanning multiple playthroughs in a modern Western setting. Although this visual novel is hardly ever discounted on Steam to attract attention from players who only buy discounted games, the engaging plot, diverse cast of characters, replayability and playing time is worth buying anytime if you like this genre of storytelling and can forgive a few minor issues in the game. Pros - Interesting narrative - Diverse cast of characters - Unlockable post-ending surprises - Guide available - Decent CGs and BGM Cons - Limited save slots - Some players may be offended by frequent use of coarse language For more reviews, join the groups and consider following the curator lists for Visual novel, JRPG, Anime and Life Needs a Little Sin [URL] [URL]

input_text: Soundboxing is in the same vein as Audioshield, but it's more about punching than deflecting. It's more beat focused than Audioshield, but at the same time it's more linear. AS sends down hits at various angles while Soundboxing is more structured delivering your hits from straight ahead of you. I like the play of Audioshield more, but Soundboxing has a great main feature that can't be ignored. The routines are all user generated. As a player you have the option to play someone else's routine or create your own challenge with the song of your choosing to share with others or play yourself. This creative layer to the game sets it apart from Audioshield or most other VR games for that matter. Audioshield is predictable, but Soundboxing is playing someone's personal choreography. Note that if the song you want isn't already set up as a challenge, you have to create it to play it. That's really not so bad though. Is one better than the other? No. Think of Audioshield as freestyle interpretive dance where Soundboxing is a planned routine. Fun either way.

input_text: You play as a Bundeswehr pilot sent to Georgia along with the recently reinstated UH-1 helicopters due to global instabilities. As you begin your duty monitoring the local infrastructure, the situation feels more and more volatile... I did this campaign after completing UN Pilot and Argo campaign. Turns out this was the right order as this is the hardest one of all three: You will push the limits of the Huey in this campaign. You're flying in IFR conditions, operating heavily loaded, using limited fuel, dropping off a squad at high altitude, doing hot and tight LZ's, temporarily entering cloud bases ... This campaign definitely will challenge you as a pilot. It is also very realistic in that it simulates airspace and radio communications. You're not the only aircraft in the area. Having previous experience in general aviation, I was pleasantly surprised at how immersed I became with the radio calls of ATC and other aircraft. The many voice-overs as well as the use of VR certainly made me feel like I was flying for the Bundeswehr along with my buddies Peter (CO), Hans and Tom (the two door gunners). Their witty comments certainly helped bring every mission alive. Some issues that I can point out so far: - radio calls would step on each other, play too early, too late leaving you confused as to what to do. - Some radio calls were very hard to understand, I had to frequently read the text. - Sometimes things went too fast so you had to take a guess as to what your next move would be. - A bug during one of the first missions where the lead helicopter is waiting for you but slowly slides into a river if you don't rush your tasking. All in all, I REALLY enjoyed this one and am looking forward to more helicopter campaigns by Low-level heaven.

input_text: Zelda: Link's Awakening is my favorite game on the original Game Boy, so buying Timothy and the Mysterious Forest was a no brainer for me when I saw the screenshots. While this game can't beat Zelda's charming overworld and clever dungeon design, I definitely had a great time playing it. The game has many familiar tile sets from Link's Awakening, including the mysterious woods, Tal Tal mountains and of course the beach where we all fell in love with Marin. :) But the gameplay is very different from anything I've played so far: Timothy doesn't have any weapons, he can only throw objects at enemies. These objects are spare, so playing stealth is a must. While a was not sure this would be fun during the entire game, it works out suprisingly well. During your quest, you meet a bunch of funny characters, and you'll have to find a wide variety of tools and items to continue. Again you'll meet familiar items like the lamp, boots and bombs, but the developers have designed brand new challenges and puzzles around them, resulting in a unique experience instead of another Zelda clone. My only point of critique is that some of the puzzles and bosses are a little too much trial and error. This can become frustrating after a while, especially because you need to be on a certain tile to trigger events. A few more hints (especially in the water dungeon) and a wider area to trigger events (at the graveyard, save crystals etc) would be a nice improvement. Tldr: Timothy and the Mysterious Forest is definitely worth playing for anyone looking for a nostalgic and/or old-school experience!

input_text: A no from me. It's very amateurish and basic. Whilst I didn't encounter the same level of bugs as the highest rated reviewer, it definitely had an unpolished feel. Even down to hilarious things like the fridge door opening into the fridge as opposed to out. But basically the whole gameplay comes down to you wandering around a forest with a few buildings, collecting items to unlock the next steps, all the while avoiding a skinless figure. The story is incredibly thin. There's only one text note I could find which would explain the backstory to this mystery figure. Once the figure caught sight of me I couldn't seem to be able to find a way to get him to stop pursuing me, so as soon as I was spotted I just flung myself into him as quickyl as possible so I could quickly reload, with minimal progress loss (provided you keep manually saving). This is the absolute wrong way to go about creating a horror. As soon as you've detoothed the monster and basically made any encounter with them revolving around seeking death as soon as possible then you've lost any sense of danger the creature could possibly have presented. Now to be fair to the game it makes it clear what you should be doing without explicitly telling you. And so I kept plowing away and kept at it until the end although I was very surprised at how quick it was to complete. It needs another area or 2 to make this worthwhile. As it stands, even at 50% off this is too much of an ask for what it is.

input_text: Inquisition is a labor of love, and it shows. However.... I have so many gripes with this game that i'm litterally grinding my teeth about it. The begining of this game took 15 hours longer than it should have, by the sole fact that the EA store app has forced its way to be a REQUIREMENT to play the game, and as with everything EA touches, it is a massive pile of shit. Over at LEAST 70 crashes total. Corrupted save files. Infinite loading screens. Skipped dialog. Missing Essential NPCs. the list could go on for hours. Then we get to the gameplay. Holy shit. WHY AM I ONLY ABLE TO HAVE 8 ABILITIES?! one of my favorite aspects of the last two games (besides the story and allies) was my ability to mix and match my spells to be extremely dynamic. instead im forced to choose 8 favorites instead of building combos out of spell interactions and ability clashes. because of this, i slowly came to hate playing my build due to the strictness of allowed abilities. speaking of being dynamicly lacking! the camera oh my GODDD. the first two games had a better camera and they came out nearly a decade before. i know that with making maps more vertical you have to change how the camera works, but i cant belive how clunky it is. and verticality? inquisition, i know your happy with yourselves for introduciing a jump button, but you really REALLY arent a platformer, stop trying to be a platformer, it makes me want to tear out my eyeballs. if i have to turn the camera around to make my character walk in a direction and youre wanting me to balance on a beam and then hop on an uneven surface that will make my inquisitor glitch halfway into the floor, all to find out that the chest at the end of the room only has a common hat and a chantry candle stub, it makes me want to throw my PC into a river. on the topic of story, there were a lot of beats i liked, some that made me stew in rage, but overall i liked the inquisitors arc. the villains are unbeliveably dumb and mustache twirly tho. I'm not the best at reviewing stories, but in the end, a lot about the lore developments didnt sit right with me. especially with how they handled the Qunari. the best part of this game for me has to be the characters, i love the main cast. their characters are endlessly charming, especially when the bicker like Varric and Cassandra. The romance was fun, but i feel like they fell a bit flat. To conclude. Good game with too many hang ups for me to fully recommend to newcomers to the series. if you want to get into dragon age, don not start with this one. start with origins. i know its rough going back to older games, but its worth it.

input_text: Instead of telling everyone how hard the game is, they should say the opposite — that it’s easy and fun to play, but also offers depth for hardcore players. They just scared away a huge audience. I heard all this myself and didn’t even want to try the game at first, especially because the tutorial is exhausting. But the game itself turned out to be better than even the developers think. You can simply pick up a weapon and swing it, knocking off other players' heads. Having a lot of fun without stressing your brain or memorizing complex moves. If the game were presented this way, it would be much more popular. And although the core gameplay is great, the game practically lacks long-term goals. All armor and weapons unlock too quickly. Because of this, the game doesn’t retain players for long. Just a few small fixes, and this could be a hit played by many people — not only geeks obsessed with medieval realism and hardcore fencing, and bored jesters.

input_text: I'm a bit hesitant to leave a positive review, but I am taking into account the alpha status at this time. This game has A LOT of potential to be really fun, I grew up on the old artillery games and this is very nostalgic for me. The physics in this game are incredible but it leaves room for a lot of problems, and this brings me to my major issue - at this time this game is WAY too hard for this engine. I cannot get passed the second level because my tank continually gets stuck in the snow and there are multiple types of enemies that are very difficult to deal with - if there were more ammo this absolutely would not be a problem because I would be able to blast my way out of these problems, but I waste most of my ammo on every weapon type just getting passed the first screen frame, and this is from being very conservative - my choice boils down to either using ammo to form the terrain so that I can actually move, or using it to destroy enemies - some of which are suicide bombers that are virtually impossible to target. I have to put this down for now until the next update unfortunately when hopefully there are some problems rectified or even some developers options put in place to have more ammo.

input_text: Abracadabrew is a very fun little game ! The point is very simple : you have to find ingredients to brew a series of potions in a very messy room. Quite simple in its core, but, as the amount of potions, ingredients and rules increase, you and your friends must find a strategy to be as efficient as possible. For me, Abracadabrew is much more a game about communication than memory. Finding a way to communicate efficiently with your partner goes a long way into completing the last levels. As you understand, I think it's a game better experienced with friends or SO. The game offers a good sense of progression, and the last levels are quite challenging, especially if you want to unlock all the witches (you need to do a much higher score in that case). The mecanic here is simple, but it works quite nicely, for us at least, to retry most of the levels for getting these cute littles witches. As I type, the game is still in early access, so they were a few technical issues. But overall, the pleasure to play is still there. And I believe that they were fixed in the first update (not tested yet, but it was in the changelog). In a more subjective matter, I also love this game because it's sweet as honey. No death, no shooting, no arch enemy, no dark topics, Only witches struggling to find the red feather and the violet eyeball for their potion. I like to shoot at pixels and to dive into dark universes as the next guy, but sometimes you need just a witchy infusion to rest a little bit.

Best enjoyed while streaming and talking with your friends while having a good time. So why am I coming back to playing these games? input_text: This game is a not bad survival game with decent graphics and sound effects, with a hard learning curve. When you need to craft things, the way it is done in this game is more realistic then in other types of this genre. And that is quite appealing. Okay, let's sum it up here a little bit... Things which makes this game interesting! - Day/Night Cycle - Equipment, lighting needs power from the generator - Different types of Equipment for manufacturing different types of items for example: (sawmill for planks, foundry unit for nails, bolts, etc..) - Once found a hatchet, start cutting that firewood - Taking a nap in your bed saves the game - Sub menus to equipment using TAB in all situations - You find a backpack, equip it so you have access to an inventory - There is a warehouse box in the basement in where you can store more items - You can dump items on the floor without them despawning, but when you save the game, there is a chance that they do dissappear. ? I have found seeds, but not the Field yet for any form of farming yet, I thought, lets dump it in the squeezer to get oil, but there is actually a small oil rig on the map. All I need to get is some form of transportation of that black liquid. I saw you can fish, like as in ingredients, so making a fish rod once the generator is running is a good idea to start with. So I was walking around and suddenly I heard a weird noise and my thought were "Oh no... Not ANOTHER zombie survival game a.k. 7 Days 2 Die??" But when I investigated the weird noise, it was actually a bear, so I was relieved! So that will be my source of meat, if I ever get a weapon of some sort. I noticed that the waterpool around the church is an instant death, so I try to avoid taking a bath in there the next time. :D Found some music albums in the basement and because the music player does not require power and the evening was already setting, I thought, let's listen to some music before bedtime (whenever available). Then nightfall eventually happened, you cannot skip the night appearantly. And then I heard some strange noises, evil laughing, growling, sounds of somebody pulling it's leg, scratching on the boardplanks, something ripping off and then footsteps... I was in the bedroom, listening to some nice Old American Songs, figuring out how to stop the music player because of the weird noises. FInally I succeeded, turned around and some half naked chick was doing the CanCan while she laughed in an evil way (same way when you got a succesful date with a woman, you pull your pants down and she points her finger to your manlyhood and starts laughing which makes you think about her honesty of being a virgin...) And then I died... Just great.... So I pressume people from a nearby loonybin have escaped and doing a murderous raid to anything and anybody they come across... I don't wanna think about zombies, like I NEVER heard a zombie laugh or doing the CanCan... -_- --- > I have not found a weapon yet, the hatchet is NOT a weapon. I did find a shit ton of ammo in the basement, but no gun or whatever. > Have not found a use-able bucket (the one from the well is firmly attached) or any form of transpot of the oil to the generator > To access utilities you need to stand near it (same as the bed) press TAB (for inventory) and you will see another menu for the other device/machine > Getting thirsty, I see water but I can't drink it. The waterwell is unaccessable. Curious what is needed to get my daily dose of water consumption. If I don't drink enough water every day, my piss will be so sour that my tube is aching for at least a few hours... Like the GUIDE says I can drink any form of water, except for the water from the cemetary... Have not figured everything out yet. I just keep on dying every night, maybe it's because I can't dance? So now I am hiding in the church in the top of the tower and waiting till the sun goes up again. I will probably fail, but I like to try out things before giving up. Had an encounter with that dreadfull bear, quite a persistent creature, kept following me wherever I went, the map is not THAT big but eventually I got rid of it. Also found deers. Another means of meat, BUT still need a weapon and most important: Drinking Water which I still haven't figured out yet. I had this idea to hide in the church tower for the night, I died because of dehydration. :P I got a real hard time on learning this game... I even tried the guide, but the guide is not telling me the things I need to know. And I found the weed... Lots of it... A little voice tells me not to take this game too serious but the other one points on all the evidence which could make this game very good. --- RECOMMENDATION = YES (especially when you look at the price...) [if the DEVELOPER still works on this game, I hope there will be options like brightness and the fact when I press OUTPUT the game is reset and back to main menu, for now I have no thoughts of improvements or whatever, I am already happy the mouse is locked in the game and it works smoothly with walking without lag - But I would not be surprised that the developer one day decided to rebuild the game from ground up, improving even better graphics with correct shadows and shadings and even more immersive crafting and collecting - For now the price is nice and low, let's see if I still think it should stay that way or need to be pumped up a notch, because the game is appealing a lot!

input_text: I enjoyed this game immensely, would recommend it to anyone. The game's one misgiving is easily out shined by the game's over all fun and awesome style. The pixel art is great, and the ambient sounds are generally pretty good. The combat itself is simplistic but not easy, and it has a certain rhythm to it that really works once you get used to it. The game very much does not hold your hand and early on its easy to wander in the 'wrong' direction and get into trouble. (This isn't a bad thing!) After I was forced to restart I found my second attempt at the game a lot easier, once I knew where things were on the map, but I definitely felt like I had earned it. (It was awesome to make my own map on paper, haven't done that in years.) That does bring up my only gripe with the game. The developers using a particular engine called AGS, and apparently every time they update it corrupts all previous saves. This isn't really acceptable in my opinion. The developers recommended not updating until you were ready, but like many people, I have steam set to auto-update. Despite this, I still recommend the game. The game is short enough you should be able to complete it between updates.

input_text: What I Like: Bought this not realizing it was only DLC. What I like is that, despite it only being DLC, it's a standalone game too, you can play it without needing the base game installed. What I Dislike: The game teases you with what you can find in other expansions. In some campaigns you're allowed to mess around and play with animals from other expansions (Which is pretty neat tbh, and not really a downside), however, this confused me once I went into freeplay and was only left with "some" of the marine animals. All others are locked, the game does not tell me why and I cannot find any information online as to why. I understand why the base game animals are not there, but when I have unlimited cash in freeplay there is no reason why all the marine animals are not available. Overall, this is a good game. At times it felt like it was trying too hard to be a zoo tycoon copy. While this game does play like a ripoff of the more major title, some parts of it are done way better (better quality animal appearences, more realistic animal interactions, the ability to choose the color you want on certain animals, guests require doctors when animals hurt them) but other features it falls short (instructions are never clear, sometimes frustratingly so, random parts of other expansions are "thrown in" as a tease but leave you more confused than in want of more (I spent 2 hours trying to figure out what to do with the researcher until I realized he couldn't do anything in my game), and controls take some getting used.) Despite the bad sides, this is an incredible competitor to Zoo Tycoon 2 and I believe if they had polished it a little more and made it more player friendly, it could have been more popular than the ever nostalgic ZT2. Reccommended for anyone seeking an alternative to Zoo Tycoon.

input_text: Spoiler-free review. From the Darkness is one of the few casual horror games that genuinely manages to scare, and it is absolutely worth playing for fans of psychological horror. Right from the beginning, the atmosphere is deeply unsettling. The player enters a seemingly abandoned building that seems empty, but with an uncanny sense that something is there. The unease builds as the main character explores the grandfather’s apartment, which, although small and made up of only a few rooms, never feels repetitive or boring. It is not claustrophobic in the traditional sense, but it creates a terrifying sense of helplessness, as if there is no way to escape should something go wrong. The horror here does not rely on constant jump scares. Most of the fear comes from the atmosphere and eerie events that slowly chip away at your sense of safety. The lack of music adds to the dread. Background audio shifts between silence and disturbing ambient noises. The sound effects all carefully chosen and realistic, no cheap or awkward noises. I want not deny that part of why I enjoyed this game is because it taps into my own personal fears and perception of horror. Since I am passionate about psychological and Victorian horror, I appreciated that the game does not rely on cheap scares or mythical monsters. Instead, it builds tension through unsettling situations and the looming presence of something unseen. What really surprised me about From the Darkness is how well-crafted it is for a casual horror game. It captures the kind of psychological dread and lasting trauma I have only felt from iconic horror filmmakers or classic games like the original Alone in the Dark and Resident Evil. As a horror enthusiast who is deeply familiar with Lovecraft, Poe, and cult classics across media, I can honestly say this game holds its own: no cheap scares, just pure, haunting atmosphere that lingers long after playing. From a technical standpoint, it holds up very well. I encountered no bugs or glitches, and the game ran smoothly on Linux, which is always a plus. From the Darkness is reasonably priced for what it offers. However, if you are unsure, waiting for a sale might be a good idea.

input_text: It's an excellently written game with excellent visual design. But, as for game design, though Breached is simple, it's rough around the edges. All core mechanics are, mostly, excellent both in their elegant simplicity and execution. The interface and navigation, landscapes and relics of a long gone civilization, all the visual and, especially, sonic stuff is brilliant. Yet an essential part of it, the Fuel Synthesis process, relies completely on chance. One cannot solve the proportion of elements as a system of equations, so there's no way around trial and error. And this element of chance gives the game its 'challenge" part, but it comes with great frustration. And a lot of replays. One minor failure can doom the playthrough. It's kinda realistic, but, man, devs, cut us some slack. A pretty, excellently written, simple game, Breached is as frustrating an experience as its bleak narrative implies. You're a lone, hopeless, broken survivor. This unforgiving game conveys that excellently.

input_text: 100% Achievement Review: A quick review based on my experience completing all the (available) achievements. Title: Super Woden GP Summary: Top-down racing game Personal notes: Super Woden GP is a old school top-down racing game. You race through different events ranging from Championships to Rally or weekend events. I found it to be very reminiscent of older Gran Turismo games but with an aerial view instead of first person. I enjoyed the classic retro art design and maps. I also enjoyed the soundtrack to a certain extent but was eventually lead to turning it off after multiple repeats. I thought that the manufacturers were well made along with a pretty extensive list of more than 70 regional cars from various points in racing history. I found the handling system to be difficult but rewarding after a slight learning curve. I ran into no issues running this game which was nice as well. Achievement-wise this game is pretty straight-forward but quite time consuming. I listed the ones I had the most difficulty with below. Two relating to the final, World Championship, while the other two are just really long distance achievements. Overall I really enjoyed my time with this game, despite the long grind for kilometres at the end of all of the events. It is a little bit of a niche genre but if you enjoy racing games I feel like you will enjoy this one, especially for its asking price. Time it took to complete: 28hrs Most difficult achievement(s): - Hardcore driver (You have won the World Championship playing on Hard level.) - Superstar (You have won the world championship with a reputation higher than 8'5.) - 3000/5000 KM! (You have driven more than 3,000/5,000 kilometers.) Difficulty rating: ★★★★★★☆☆☆☆ 6/10 Overall rating: ★★★★★★★☆☆☆ 7/10

input_text: Greatly inspired by Journey, Loop is a hidden gem of a puzzle game. Loop is a "zen game" focused on telling a beautiful story through its eye-watering visuals and fantastic music. - Oh right, the music! The music alone could be enough of a reason to buy the game. If you watched the show "Made in Abyss" (best anime of 2017), you would know what type of music I'm talking about! All through the game it was giving me goosebumps. - The gameplay is relaxing and easy to learn, but since it is a puzzle game you will need to use your head to progress. Don't expect nothing incredibly difficult though, as it is focused more on the jorney of the characters and players. -The story is cleverly told without any dialog, just how the characters act and react. I don't wan't to spoil any of it but it got me hooked! -The controls are as good and easy as they get! Together with the sound effects, it makes you feel satisfied with every action you perform! I think the game is really worth the price, so please give it a chance!

input_text: A modern-ish feeling dungeon crawler with a save system that's only as punishing as your paranoia. If you are directionally challenged like I am, there is also certainly a learning curve to its level design. Lunacid has a modern-retro style that oozes a clear admiration for all things cosmic horror and FromSoftware, with some other very clear and interesting homages and plenty of the developers own incredible sense of atmosphere and style. As someone riding the intense high and moderate frustration of fully completing the game and unlocking all its endings, most of it is of the level of frustration that comes from simply acclimating to the game's difficulty and mastering the mechanics to completion. That being said, to unlock the final ending you must find every weapon and every spell in the game. This includes upgrading weapons to different forms, which in itself can be a time consuming endeavor. This would be fine and manageable, even considering the game's intentionally obtuse level design, if this completion process did not involve farming items off enemies that spawn in incredibly small, specific areas. I am happy to hug walls and mash E because the sound of gravel lifting from the ground is music to my ears. I am not happy to have to trudge back to fight three guys that have a less than ten percent chance to drop the item that I need. I gripe about this because after experiencing everything the game has to offer and getting the final, full completion ending, I am over the moon (heh), that I did. There were so many moments where the combination of the game's intensely cultivated atmosphere and beautiful soundtrack left me so appreciative that this game caught my eye. The developer's penchant for reaching out beyond the veil for the handful of secret endings and goodies you find that lead up to them were a delight to try and uncover, and inevitably Google when I couldn't figure out exactly how to stand in one specific puddle. Please give this game a chance if you love FromSoft games from any generation, but especially if you are as constantly hungry for amazing pieces of cosmic horror media as I am, as this will forever be one of my favorite entries in that genre, plain and simple.

input_text: I know this game is marked as adult only, but it's not really explicit. TurretGirls is a genuinely well made, fun to play on rails shooter with censored nudity that only happens if you lose by one of two ways. The gameplay is simple. You are on a railroad track with a giant turret and your operator, a petite woman. You shoot aliens that are trying to destroy generators located below you, while a small subset of those aliens instead try to attack your operator. Each wave you win you get money to spend on adding weapons to your turret, upgrading your stats or adding/replacing generators. Each generator gives power to a superweapon for each wave you win. Completely power the super weapon and you face a boss that ends the level. The ONLY part of this game that is actually adult is this: When you take damage your operators clothes get damaged and destroyed. On low health your character starts to pant as if exhausted, and if you lose all your health she has no clothes on, but it's all censored. Then you get a static loss screen of her censored body being surrounded by aliens, with no genitalia or penetration or anything. She speaks but it's mildly suggestive at best, not explicit. Plus if you lose by having your generators destroyed, then the loss screen is entirely un-suggestive. Also, the game has an actual progression system where you unlock starting turrets and clothing that offers differing stats. The gunplay feels smooth and while it's not the most difficult game it's nice. It's a good game to just shut your brain off and shoot things. The audio design is actually quality, with the mechanical weapon sounds being a great standout. I know for most "adult" games the gameplay standard is very low, but this game has some actual substance to it and I appreciate that. Honestly, if the game didn't have complete clothing destruction and the suggestive end screen, the game probably wouldn't be marked as NSFW. Heck, I'd prefer if it wasn't marked as NSFW so that I didn't have to have people look at me weird for recommending it so vehemently. It's a very solid, well made game that is worth playing.

The fucking laptop, playing this game you can spend at least a fourth of your game time on it, be it trying to solve sixteen panels sliding puzzles (who thought that was fun really ?), answering quizz about "on what day did this character say that to you ?" A lot of the dialog in this game is very repetitive, even during one dialog a lot of it is rephrasing what was just said before in another way (to make sure you remember it I guess ?) and I felt like this stretched the game too much. We could have gained a much better pacing just getting rid of the same thing being said twice or more. I'll finish my rant here because I do recommend this game, lots of fun, lots of babes. A lot of potential. We'll see how it evolves for the next updates.

It's the same missions with only slight differences in equipment until you have the specialized vehicles which makes the missions trivial, which is boring. I enjoy this game, however it needs more content and it could really use procedural generation for missions to make no two alike, even if they use the same small selection of maps. Difficulty level was not challenging. Once you understand how to do a mission quickly, it becomes dull. When I saw the train derailment mission, I thought "wow this will be fun". Then I go there with my foam tender and spray one small fire and complete the mission in less time than it took for the mission to load. That is disappointing. The game is much more fun if you let everything catch on fire for a while, let the injured people almost die, then start fighting the fires. I felt like I had cool equipment and vehicles, but really didn't feel like I was using them. Often, I could bust into a fire with 4 people using fire extinguishers and avoid all of the fun of setting up hoses. However, I am still recommending this game because it is suitably polished. It's good for about a day's worth of play and good for kids to play with parents. This is an improvement over the previous Rescue. The game design and engine have enormous potential, but the content is currently (6/5/2015) mediocre.

input_text: One of the better Choice Of games in their lineup, but not without its flaws. Definitely no Choice of Robots or Heroes Rise, but definitely worth a read through if you're a fan of these types of games. Being a fan of cats helps a lot too. The good is in the writing's humor. I found myself laughing out loud a few times from delivery alone. The author does a great job at weaving complex stories and monologues into everyday feline antics, providing a different perspective into human way of life that gets you feeling like you're actually in the head of a freshly introduced housecat. However, the story does end up dragging on in the later chapters, straight up to its sudden ending. There wasn't any sort of conclusion to be had save for an awkward recapping of your statistics and choices, which left me disappointed. There are different paths, scenes, and achievements to find in replays, but ugh... the lack of closure hurts me. As for the stat-based gameplay aspect, I've found to be... not great. There were far too many to keep track of and the way they affect choices and how the choices affect them were unclear. Does sitting still check your comfort/fun-loving, feral/domestication, or audacity/caution? Perhaps obeying makes it check loyalty instead? What about your jumping ability? For better or worse, the writing does weave failure and success of the stat-checks quite well into the narrative and it's difficult to tell sometimes if there had even been one at all or if it had even mattered. I'd chalk that up to good storytelling, but it may irk some readers. My advice is to just play through the story (at least once) without worrying too much about the inner workings. Or if you insist on min-maxing, choose the options that portray the cat that you want to be, as they tend to be fairly consistent: how active you are, how selfish, or how loving, etc. Whatever you choose to do, the story won't fault you for it. And hey, even if you're all over the board, you'll be all the more cat-like in your unpredictability. Not bad. Solid pick, but not the best.

input_text: Sherlock Holmes: The Awakened is a full remake of the 2007 title by Frogwares, rebuilt from the ground up in Unreal Engine 4. It’s both a detective adventure and a Lovecraftian horror story, blending Arthur Conan Doyle’s iconic characters with the cosmic dread of H.P. Lovecraft. The game serves as a continuation of Sherlock Holmes: Chapter One, exploring Holmes’ early career alongside Dr. Watson. The narrative begins as a standard Holmes mystery in Victorian London, but it quickly spirals into something darker. Holmes and Watson investigate a series of kidnappings, uncovering a sinister cult obsessed with the Great Old Ones. The writing walks a fine line between classic detective storytelling and supernatural horror. Holmes is portrayed as brilliant but haunted, struggling with doubt and obsession. Watson acts as both partner and anchor, grounding the story. The Lovecraftian themes are eerie but not overly grotesque, leaning more into psychological tension than gore. Players collect clues, analyze evidence, interrogate suspects, and use Holmes’ deduction board to piece together solutions. Environments range from London streets to Louisiana swamps and Swiss asylums, each atmospheric and unsettling. The game relies on logic puzzles, observation, and connecting evidence rather than combat. Holmes’ mind can fracture under the weight of the horrors he uncovers, adding tension to the investigations. The Unreal Engine remake gives the game detailed environments and improved character models, though animations can feel stiff at times. Sherlock Holmes: The Awakened is a compelling detective adventure that successfully blends classic mystery with cosmic horror. While not flawless in execution, it delivers an immersive story, strong atmosphere, and a fresh take on Holmes’ early years. For fans of Sherlock, Lovecraft, or narrative-driven mysteries, it’s a rewarding experience. 8/10 DISASTER | BAD | MEDIOCRE | OKAY | GOOD | GREAT |AMAZING| MASTERPIECE Reviewed on: Win11 Home 64-bit, Intel i5-11600K, GeForce RTX 3060 Ti 8GB TUF, 32GB DDR4-3600 RAM, 2 x Kingston NV1 1TB M.2 NVMe SSD, Internet Broadband 1000/1000 Mbit If you like this review, then please consider giving it a thumbs up. I also was a heavier kid and was so amazed to see a game have a chubby girl as the main character. Not a side character.. not an antagonist or someone to laugh at.. A. MAIN. CHARACTER! input_text: A Roxy Raccoon Universe game without raccoons! Instead, we have a Hotline Miami meets dungeon maze (?) entry into the series. Not my usual style of game, but was fun. Game play wise, you have 35 normal levels and several boss levels. Normal levels you'll sneak through the dungeons, avoiding traps, witches, and goblins. You'll also need to use an arsenal of weapons to get by. Different ones are available throughout the game and more unlock as you go, I believe there are 10 or so in total. They don't have names, but I really like the weaker fly homing spells, and the firework spread spell. The game gets harder as you go along, but also introduces some enemy-less levels later on that I found to be a nice break. Boss battles usually are in an arena type battle where you get a few choice of weapons to deal with them. They are fairly straight forward, and you get an achievement for each. Speaking of achievements, they are for completing the story, watching credits at the end, playing various mini games, and a couple about time and amount of kills in levels. No achievement is particularly difficult. I really liked some music on the levels, the sounds match what I am doing. I never got annoyed by anything sound wise either. But it's also not particularly noteworthy. Story wise, this focuses on Donna. Introducing us to the other witches and her family. We learn a bit more about her, and that this is a prequel to Roxy Raccoon. Dev added a few accessibility options that I asked for that made the game much better for me. They are always open to requests like this, and that is very important to me.

input_text: Full disclosure: I got this game on sale for .49 cents USD. It's, um, rather unusual. Do you remember being a kid and wanting to celebrate Halloween, but maybe your grandmother never did and just didn't "get" it? But still, she was your gran, so you'd get something, right? That something didn't make any more sense that the Christmas candy corn or shamrocks in this collection, but she tried. Kind of. That's what this puzzle collection plays like. Considering Halloween started as a harvest festival of Samhain, a lot of the photos are technically correct, and a quite a few even have Halloween imagery. But some are just off, like what might be a tropical crow and green cupcakes. It's kind of a let down as the Easter collection was spot on, and matched all my childhood memories, so the celebrations must be pretty universal. But something was lost in translation here. Some of the photos are worth the .49 cents USD to me, but it must be a cultural thing with the grey cat and peppy upbeat music. Worth it on sale if you like what you see, just don't expect this collection to make as much sense as usual. And I apologize if people from different parts of the world indeed celebrate just like this and it's not computing with my American brain. EDIT: OK, having played for more time, this is one of their weaker collections. Technically yes, plain pumpkins or corn can make Halloween decor. But Day of the Dead and Thanksgiving wandered in, along with somebody's pet husky-wolf hybrids that are in a fenced off area. It just doesn't feel like they tried, but I got the collection for the cute witch closeup and witchy hot air balloon.
